source_text: Rem quae in subiecto est, sine illa re esse non posse, in qua subiecta est. Et ideo, putas, malum quod est in parente, utique in subiecto, alii rei, id est proli, ad quam non pervenit, reatum non posse transmittere
pass_a_gloss: Rem which in subiecto is, without that re to-be not to-be-able, in where subiecta is. and for-that-reason, putas, evil that/which is in parente, utique in subiecto, alii guilty, it is proli, to than/which not pervenit, reatum not to-be-able transmittere.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: A thing existing in a subject cannot exist without the thing in which it inheres. Therefore the evil in a parent, existing in that subject, cannot transmit guilt to another thing—the offspring—to which it has not passed.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
